adds `test/playwright/unit/core/Util.spec.mjs` for `createStyleObject()` and `createStyles()`: several declarations, trailing semicolon, `data:` url with a semicolon, `http:` url with a colon, kebab to camel, numeric values, null/undefined skipping and the round trip. those six passed on untouched source. then moved the three inline regexes to documented static members next to `decamelRegEx` and dropped the todo. one more test pins the new members. no behaviour change.

Resolves #20670

# PR Micro-Review

**Opening**: Thank you, @tridev-tej. You wrote the six behaviour tests first and saw them pass on the untouched source before moving a single regex, and that order is what turns "no behaviour change" from a claim into a fact. Neo is an [application engine](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/learn/benefits/Introduction.md). Your change sits in `Neo.core.Util`, the static helpers that turn style strings into objects and back. To run the engine locally, see [Set up the engine from a clone](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md#set-up-the-engine-from-a-clone); for a next one, see [good first issue](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/labels/good%20first%20issue).

**Class:** mechanical — a test-only addition plus the behaviour-preserving move that #20670 prescribed: three inline patterns become documented static members beside `decamelRegEx`. No concept is introduced.

**Verdict:** Approved

**Glance:** I checked the diff at `4af35e4812` against #20670's four ACs.
- **AC-1 and AC-2:** the seven tests cover each named case, including the `data:` URL with its inner semicolon, the `http:` URL with its inner colon, `10px` staying a string and the `createStyles` round trip.
- **AC-3:** `createStyleObject()` now uses `Util.styleDeclarationRegEx`, `Util.stylePropertyRegEx` and `Util.camelRegEx`. Each matches the inline pattern it replaces character for character and takes `decamelRegEx`'s JSDoc shape, and the `TODO` is gone.
- **AC-4, run as a falsifier:** I ran the new spec against `dev`'s untouched `Util.mjs`. The six behaviour tests pass, and only the static-members test fails, as it must before the move.

The one thing I looked for: shared `/g` regexes can carry `lastIndex` from one call into the next, but only `exec` and `test` keep that state. `split` and `replace`, the only uses here and `decamelRegEx`'s precedent, reset it. No site outside the prescription is touched, and CI is green at the head.
